claim: OVRLAP walks the NCENT segment slots looking for a segment this head overlaps. ENTRY (X)=index of head; EXIT carry SET if an overlap occurs.
OVRLAP only counts a candidate on the SAME scan line: it compares MOBJV[Y] against MOBJV[X] and skips (30$) when they differ.
OVRLAP skips a DEAD segment or a floating SCORE: a candidate whose colour MOBJC >= 0xC0 is ignored (this is why EXPLOD parks a finished score at colour 0xFF, MS-13).
OVRLAP never counts the head against itself: the candidate index Y is compared to the entry index (TEMP1=X) and skipped when equal (DO NOT COUNT US).
OVRLAP looks only AHEAD: it EORs the H-difference with the head's own MOBJDH so the in-front direction is normalised regardless of which way the head marches (LOOK ONLY IN FRONT OF US).

source.verbatim: EOR X,MOBJDH		;LOOK ONLY IN FRONT OF US

claim: OVRLAP declares an overlap when the direction-normalised H-difference is within the 0xF4 wrap window (BCS 40$ sets carry): a segment close ahead on the same line overlaps.
The split: a millipede reaching the bottom row (V < 9) triggers the promotion of its body tail to a fresh head (16$ '.. IF NOT AT BOTTOM').
The split promotes the tail of the body run (colour 0x3D bodies) to a new HEAD: MOBJC of the tail slot is set to 0x39 ('TURN ON COLOR FOR EYES') — a body becomes a head, so the train splits in two.

source.verbatim: STA Y,MOBJC		;TURN ON COLOR FOR EYES

claim: The newly-promoted head REVERSES its horizontal direction: the tail's MOBJDH is complemented (JSR COMP) before it is stored (REVERSE HDIR).
The newly-promoted head does NOT descend for one line: its MOBJDV is set to 0 ('DV=0 FOR ONE LINE'); a tail which just split should not immediately turn.
The promoted head's V is snapped onto a clean cell line before it becomes a head (ADC I,04 / AND I,0F8 — 'BE SURE TAIL STARTS ON THE RIGHT LINE').

source.verbatim: STA Y,MOBJV		;BE SURE TAIL STARTS ON THE RIGHT LINE

claim: EXPLOD sweeps all 16 motion-object slots (LDX I,15. — indices 0..15); the exploding player uses the last slot (15).

source.verbatim: EXPLOD:	LDX I,15.		;EXPLODING MUSHROOMS USES PLAYER'S SLOT

claim: A finished explosion that displays a score parks the slot at colour 0xFF so OVRLAP will not treat it as a collidable segment (SET COLOR SO 'OVRLAP' DOES NOT DETECT COLLISION).

source.verbatim: STA X,MOBJC		;SET COLOR SO "OVRLAP" DOES NOT DETECT COLLISION

claim: A displayed score is held on screen for a delay of 0xA0 (LEAVE SCORE OUT FOR AWHILE) before the slot is cleared.

source.verbatim: LDA I,0A0		;LEAVE SCORE OUT FOR AWHILE

claim: The player explosion runs off the PEXPLD countdown: EXPLOD decrements PEXPLD every frame it is called, and ends the explosion when it reaches 0.

Player-explosion phase 1 (PEXPLD in 0x50..0x60) is the FLASHING-COLORS phase: the ROM writes BKGND (full-screen background colour) each frame. This is the photosensitive-strobe hazard the freeze-friendly redesign (AC-4) must neutralise — the clone must NOT cycle a full-screen background here.
Player-explosion phase 2 (PEXPLD in 0x20..0x50) is the SPARKLE phase: the ROM writes PLAYC (the player's own colour), a localised effect, not a full-screen flash.
Player-explosion phase 3 (PEXPLD below 0x20) is the DYING sequence: the ROM writes PLAYP (the player picture) to collapse the player.
PLAY classifies the object as a SPIDER when SPDP is in the range 0x14..0x1C (a spider gets a wider, V-weighted hit box). Millipede segments are non-spiders and use the tight box.
PLAY (non-spider): a collision is impossible once the horizontal distance |objH - playerH| reaches 6 (CMP I,06 / BCS 25$ returns no-collision).
PLAY: a collision is impossible once the vertical distance |objV - playerV| reaches 6 (CMP I,6 / BCS 25$).
PLAY: the final hit test sums the axis distances (H + V, or H + 2*V for a spider) and requires the sum below 0x0A to register a hit (CMP I,0A / BCS 25$ is a miss).
On a player hit PLAY arms the player explosion by storing 0x60 into PEXPLD (EXPLOSION SOUND FOR PLAYER) — the countdown MS-15/16/17/18 then plays out, and PLAY returns carry-clear (collision).
A segment explosion picture counts down and is FINISHED at the 0xFA floor (CPY I,0FA): pictures above 0xFA are still exploding and DEC toward it. EXPLODE_DONE = 0xFA.
PLAY's SPIDER horizontal box is wider than a segment's: a spider collision is possible while the horizontal distance is below 10. (decimal) — CMP I,10. / BCC 15$. SPIDER_HIT_DH_MAX = 10.

PLAY's axis distance is a ONE'S-complement absolute value, not a true abs: after the byte subtract, a negative result is folded with a bare EOR I,0FF (no +1 — that would be the two's-complement COMP at MLIRQ.MAC:630, which PLAY does NOT call). The ROM comment says it: '-10 BECOMES +9'. So a negative delta reads one pixel short, making the hit box asymmetric by a pixel. CKFF (XORed first) is 0 upright, so this is not cocktail-only.

On a player hit PLAY also sets DELAY to 0x10 (a delay before the next object setup). This is a game-loop timer, wired with scoring/setup (ml5); it is documented here but not consumed by the ml3-2 pure reducers.

source.verbatim: STA DELAY		;SET DELAY BEFORE NEXT SETUP
